_about: Lane C. Ipsos final pre-election polls for 2016 and 2019. Both finals' full SMH article bodies were captured live from smh.com.au (the page embeds the complete body in its GraphQL asset payload — paywall does not gate the JSON). Poll Bludger relays saved as cross-checks. NEITHER final printed state/age/gender voting-intention breakdowns in these sources; the only sub-total printed is the 2019 already-voted cohort.

waves.finding: final Fairfax-Ipsos poll of the 2016 election (SMH/The Age, 'Dead heat on election eve as final poll points to cliffhanger', Mark Kenny; first published 2016-06-30)
waves.method: nationwide survey by telephone (Ipsos for Fairfax)
waves.note: Headline 50-50 is the 2013-election preference-flow basis; respondent-allocated preferences give Labor 51-49 (SMH: 'identical outcome to that returned in the last two fortnightly Fairfax-Ipsos polls'; a 4.5 per cent swing to Labor since 2013). Primaries: 'Coalition primary vote sits at 40' (up 1), Labor 33 ('persistently low'), Greens 13 (down 1); SMH prints the combined 'Greens and other crossbench parties and independents' at 27% → others 14 implied (Wikipedia's table row prints Others 14 explicitly). One Nation/NXT not broken out by Ipsos. Fieldwork window per SMH 'between Sunday June 26 and Wednesday 29'; the Poll Bludger relay says 'conducted Monday to Wednesday' — SMH kept as the primary-source window (26-29 Jun). PPM Turnbull 49-35. Approvals: Turnbull 49/41 (net +8), Shorten 42/50. Expectations: 'some 6 in 10 voters declared they expect Malcolm Turnbull to be returned, compared to just 17 per cent who think Bill Shorten will win'.

waves.finding: final Ipsos poll for the ex-Fairfax papers (SMH/The Age, 'Ipsos poll shows election contest tightens to 51-49', David Crowe; published 2019-05-16)
waves.method: telephone, 46 per cent of the sample mobile; margin of error 2.3% (SMH)

Already voted (early voters).note: primaries printed as '41 per cent said they were Coalition voters while 33 per cent favoured Labor'; 2PP 'those who have already voted favour the Coalition over Labor by 53 to 47 per cent'; 'almost one third of voters told Ipsos they had voted early or intended to do so'

waves.note: 2PP identical 51-49 to Labor on BOTH bases (2016-election-flow basis allocates One Nation and UAP preferences 53-47 to the Coalition; respondent-allocated also 51-49). Primaries printed sum 92 (39+33+13+4+3); remaining ~8% (undecided + other parties) NOT printed in either the SMH body or the PB relay — oth filed null rather than derived. Approvals: Morrison 48/43 (net +5), Shorten 43/48 (net −5); PPM Morrison leads 47-40 (PB relay; SMH body confirms the lead, numbers in PB). Expectation of winner: ALP 55 / Coalition 32 / undecided 13.

sources.note: PRIMARY SOURCE: SMH final 2016 Ipsos article, full body captured live
PB relay cross-check of the 2016 Ipsos final (also carries the Galaxy final — see lanes/galaxy.json)

sources.archived: src/ipsos/smh-2019-05-16-ipsos-51-49.html (+ -body.txt extracted body; amp variant fetched identical)
sources.note: PRIMARY SOURCE: SMH final 2019 Ipsos article, full body captured live
PB relay cross-check of the 2019 Ipsos final (adds 'conducted Sunday to Wednesday', n=1842, ON/UAP flow detail)

notes: Row sums: 2016 final 40+33+13+14=100 (others component derived/confirmed by Wikipedia; SMH prints only the 27% combined non-major figure and the three named parties). 2019 final printed figures sum 92 with ~8 unprinted — flagged rather than derived, per never-invent rule.

Neither final printed state/age/gender VI breakdowns in any open source: the 2016 SMH article embeds Fairfax's 'yourvote' election interactive (theage.com.au/interactive/2016/yourvote/v17/index.html) which is the only plausible carrier of state splits for 2016, and it was not retrievable this pass (live interactive is Flash-era and Wayback was offline).

Ipsos's own ipsos.com/en-au post-election releases (e.g. the 2016 'Election Review' and 2019 post-mortems) carry leader-approval and issues material, not demographic VI tables; checked via web search, nothing fetchable at ipsos.com for these waves.
gaps: State/age/gender splits for both finals — not printed by Fairfax/SMH/The Age in either year and not relayed by Poll Bludger; the only sub-total in print is the 2019 early-voter cohort (filed). Probe lines: theage interactive 'yourvote/v17' (2016, interactive iframe, needs Wayback — IA offline all pass); Ipsos Australia press office never published crosstub PDFs for these waves.
2019 final: the ~8pt unprinted remainder (undecided + other parties) — Ipsos-era Fairfax practice was to report decideds; the residual split was not published in the captured sources.
